corrected_draft.description_long: On March 11, 2025, the U.S. Department of Education announced that it had initiated a reduction in force affecting nearly half of its workforce and that impacted employees would be placed on administrative leave. The department’s release described its workforce as 4,133 at the start of the administration and projected roughly 2,183 after the actions. That projection included employees who had already accepted voluntary separation programs as well as the new RIF. The Department of Education Office of Inspector General later reported staffing changes in 16 of 17 offices and an overall reduction of at least 1,579 of 3,902 employees by March 31, 2025: 1,227 employees separated through RIF actions and at least 352 through voluntary options. GAO separately documented that about half of the Office for Civil Rights staff were placed on paid administrative leave and that later court orders affected the RIF. The original statement that DOGE fired 1,300 employees should be replaced with an accurately attributed announcement and counts distinguishing positions affected, completed RIF separations, and voluntary departures.

corrected_draft.description_medium: Trump Media & Technology Group planned a paid Truth API feed offering early access to Trump’s Truth Social posts for up to $100,000 per month. corrected_draft.description_long: Trump Media & Technology Group announced a paid, licensed Truth API feed intended to give banks and trading firms faster access to posts from the ten most influential Truth Social accounts. Reuters reported that, before the launch, the company had discussed charging up to $100,000 per month, or $60,000 monthly for a three-year commitment. Reuters also reported that the company said customers had signed up ahead of launch, but did not identify them; the reported offer prices came from unnamed sources. The product raises questions about whether financial firms can receive Trump’s posts before ordinary users and news outlets, particularly when posts announce tariffs or other government actions. A press-freedom group and a media outlet later sued, arguing that the feed sold government information; Trump Media responded that the posts were widely available. The sources establish a commercial data product and reported pricing, but they do not provide an official determination that each post is a presidential record or establish that the service violated records law. The legal status of the posts and the boundaries between the company’s feed and government records remain unresolved.
